title: M7 · The shared history line
intro: Every person's summary ends with one line, History · N changes ›, as the design review decided (rulebook v1.010, picture 09b): a tap opens the list in place, newest first — what changed, then when · who. Each section reads its own history and writes its own “what changed”; the line writes the date and the name the same way everywhere (“Oct 22 · Jeffrey Berg”, Massachusetts time). Amber outline = what the shared line decides. Two details to OK: (a) the arrow points right (›) while closed and down while open — the icon list keeps › for “go to a page”, so the new row records this one use; (b) the states the design review's drawing didn't show (4–6): “Loading…” while it reads; the amber bar with Retry if it can't read (today Star shows “No changes recorded yet.”, which hides the problem); “History · no changes yet” as plain text when there is nothing. Every state at all four sizes: M7-history-line.png.

sections.head: As the summary opens — detail (a): the arrow points right (›)
Open — detail (a): the arrow points down
Detail (b): while it reads, if it can't read, and nothing yet (PC; every size is on the full sheet)

footer: What changes for each section when it switches (later, in its own prompt): Color Belt (event and private testing), Camps and Black Belt gain the line — each first needs a database reader for its own history, with a security review (v1.010) · Star's five-row block becomes the line, and its dates lose the year and the time of day (today “Oct 22, 2026, 4:05 PM”; the approved drawing writes “Oct 22”) · Prospects keeps its own (v1.010); its dates are taken in UTC today, a small bug for Prospects' prompt.
